2610.13303.title: Agreement Without Alignment: Label-Free Rubric Clarification Increases LLM-Judge Consensus but Not Agreement with Humans
2610.13303.paper_summary: LLM judges are increasingly deployed as panels, and disagreement among panel members is often read as a symptom of an unclear rubric. We test a label-free procedure that turns this disagreement into rubric repairs. The procedure decomposes each rubric into sub-criteria, ranks them by cross-judge disagreement on a development split, and has an editor model rewrite only the most contested ones. An additional stage that moves text-checkable sub-criteria to deterministic checkers transferred none in our evaluation. Human labels are never used to select or edit clauses; they are used only to evaluate the outcome. We pre-specified four hypotheses in a version-controlled protocol and evaluated six rubric conditions with a panel of five judges from three providers on SummEval, the HealthBench meta-evaluation, and USR Topical-Chat, for a total of 129,770 judge requests, excluding retries. On SummEval, the procedure raised inter-judge Krippendorff's $α$ by 0.069 (95% CI 0.046 to 0.092) over the original rubric and by 0.074 over a control that applied the same edits to an equal number of randomly chosen clauses that were not selected. Agreement with expert ratings showed no detectable change (Kendall $τ$ difference -0.007, 95% CI -0.037 to 0.021). On HealthBench and USR, neither inter-judge agreement nor human agreement met the preregistered effect criteria. In a preregistered secondary comparison, human agreement after editing the contested clauses was lower than after editing the control clauses on all three datasets in point estimate, although no interval excluded zero. Selecting clauses by disagreement makes judges agree with each other more than editing arbitrary clauses does, but in our setting the added consensus did not bring the judges closer to human annotators. We will release code, frozen rubrics, item identifiers, and judge scores.
2610.13303.paper_summary_zh: LLM 評審團越來越多地以小組形式部署，而小組成員之間的分歧通常被解讀為不明確的評分標準的症狀。<lb/>我們測試了一種無標籤的程序，將這種分歧轉化為評分標準的修正。<lb/>該程序將每個評分標準分解為子標準，根據發展分割中評審之間的分歧對其進行排名，並讓編輯模型僅重寫最具爭議的部分。<lb/>一個額外的階段將可檢查的子標準移至確定性檢查者，但在我們的評估中沒有轉移任何內容。<lb/>人類標籤從未用於選擇或編輯條款；它們僅用於評估結果。<lb/>我們在版本控制的協議中預先指定了四個假設，並在 SummEval、HealthBench 元評估和 USR Topical-Chat 上評估了六個評分標準條件，參與者為來自三個提供者的五名評審，總共進行了 129,770 次評審請求，不包括重試。<lb/>在 SummEval 上，該程序將評審之間的 Krippendorff $α$ 提高了 0.069（95% CI 0.046 至 0.092），超過了原始評分標準，並在對照組中提高了 0.074，該對照組對同樣數量的隨機選擇的未被選擇的條款應用了相同的編輯。<lb/>與專家評分的一致性顯示沒有可檢測的變化（Kendall $τ$ 差異 -0.007，95% CI -0.037 至 0.021）。<lb/>在 HealthBench 和 USR 中，評審之間的一致性和人類一致性均未達到預註冊的效果標準。<lb/>在一項預註冊的次要比較中，編輯爭議條款後的人類一致性在所有三個數據集中的點估計上均低於編輯對照條款後的結果，儘管沒有區間排除零。<lb/>根據分歧選擇條款使評審之間的共識比編輯任意條款更高，但在我們的設定中，增加的共識並未使評審更接近人類標註者。<lb/>我們將發布代碼、凍結的評分標準、項目標識符和評審分數。
